claims.text: The starting catalyst is a homogeneous solid-solution alloy containing several principal elements in nearly equiatomic concentrations and a low fraction of platinum-group metals.
A combined thermal-annealing and acid-etching dealloying treatment can produce a Pt-rich shell around a PtCoFeNiCu high-entropy-alloy core.
The Pt-rich shell produced by the treatment will be ultra-thin.
The nitrogen anneal can be performed at low temperature while still producing the proposed shell and nitrogen incorporation.
Acidic dealloying selectively removes less noble or less stable metals from the alloy.
Selective dealloying drives platinum segregation toward the catalyst surface.
Nitrogen incorporation creates multiple metal–nitrogen bonds in the treated catalyst.
The treatment leaves an intact high-entropy-alloy core surrounded by a nanoscale Pt-rich shell.
Metal–nitrogen bonding reinforces the Pt-rich shell and improves corrosion resistance, activity, and durability.
The combined high-entropy core, Pt-rich shell, and metal–nitrogen bonds beneficially modify the catalyst's electronic or core structure.
The modified shell protects the catalyst against sintering.
The modified shell protects the catalyst against oxidation and poisoning by exhaust constituents such as H2O and NO.
The untreated catalyst loses activity over time under transient, low-temperature automotive exhaust conditions.
Structural dealloying or surface dissolution contributes to degradation of multimetallic catalysts under reaction conditions.
Sintering and poisoning by H2O and NO cause degradation of the untreated catalyst.

Relative to the untreated catalyst, the treated catalyst will retain greater catalytic activity and durability during transient, low-temperature gasoline or hybrid-vehicle exhaust operation, including H2O and NO exposure and mileage-like thermal cycling.
The proposed performance improvement can be achieved while using less platinum overall.
Performance benefits require fine tuning of acid concentration, etching duration, and nitrogen-annealing temperature and may disappear far outside typical exhaust conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes the low-temperature nitrogen anneal as optional, whereas the intervention specifies acid etching followed by nitrogen annealing as the required treatment.
